title: Repair an evidence-first NSX Policy connectivity diagnostic client
prompt:
A VCF 9.1 operations integration is misdiagnosing a failed connectivity trace as a firewall problem before it has collected any evidence. Repair the single-file Java implementation in NsxPolicyClient.java. The public records and diagnoseConnectivityFailure(String) signature must remain compatible with TestMain. Derive request behavior from docs/contract.json, which was extracted from the pinned official NSX Policy OpenAPI specification identified in docs/official_sources.json.

For one diagnosis, pull the realized-state alarm events with ListAlarms and then the named traceflow's observation log with ListTraceflowObservations. Return every alarm whose severity is ERROR as AlarmEvidence and every TraceflowObservationDropped or TraceflowObservationDroppedLogical item as DropEvidence, preserving response order and the response values used by the public records. Do not infer or hard-code a root-cause label: the report is the collected evidence.

Build the operation paths under the contract's /policy/api/v1 base path. Treat traceflow-id as one RFC 3986 UTF-8 path segment (spaces are %20 and a slash inside the ID is %2F). The optional query parameters in the contract are unset in this workflow and must be omitted entirely, not serialized with empty values. Send both requests as GET with Accept: application/json and HTTP Basic authorization from the constructor credentials. A non-2xx response or malformed response must fail the diagnosis instead of returning guessed evidence. Use only the JDK; do not add dependencies or contact a live VMware endpoint. Run python3 test/verify.py to check the implementation.
scenario: replace a guessed firewall diagnosis with real ListAlarms ERROR events and ListTraceflowObservations drop records collected over the pinned NSX Policy contract
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves both GET targets, RFC 3986 traceflow-id segment encoding, omitted optional queries, and Basic authorization byte-for-byte
